text:
Hochwohlgebohrner Herr
Hochzuverehrender Herr Kriegs und ForstRath!
Ich habe die Ehre Euer Hochwohlgebohren noch einiges
was mit heutiger reutenden Post von dem e. H. Glenck
eingegangen ist mitzutheilen, das fürstliche Schreiben
hatte ich bereits zur Post gegeben, als ich von des
Fürsten Durchlaucht den Befehl erhielte im Nach¬
trag das zu sagen, was ich hier im Auszug abschrifft-
lich anlege. Sr Durchlaucht glauben, daß es denen¬
selben von Nutzen seyn dürfte. Höchstdieselben
befinden sich heute besser als gestern, in dem der
Anfall aus der rechten Hand in den linken Fuß
gezogen war, und gestern dort heftig schmerz¬
te, jedoch hörte dieser Schmerz diese Nacht auf
und war sogar beym ausdehnen der Sehnen

nicht mehr fühlbar, mir hoffen alle das besten.
Herr Bergrath Bernhardi iſt für angekommen, jedoch
wie ich gestern selbst sahe - nicht ganz geſund - Sr
Durchlaucht schikten mich, um Ihn darüber zu beru¬
higen, weil Er wegen seiner fortdauernden Unpä¬
lichkeit noch nicht seine Aufwartung machen konnte.
Euer Hochwohlgebohren erlauben mir noch schlieslich
den herzlichsten Wunsch Ihrer Wiederstellung
und vollkommensten Fortdauernden Geſundheit
anzuhängen, und zugleich mich deren ferneren un¬
schäzbaren Gewogenheit empfehlen zu dürfen
Stets in vollkommenster Verehrung.
Euer Hochwohlgebohren,
Breslau d 8ten Mertz
1805.
unterthäniger Diener
A. Hahn

translation.en:
Right Honourable Sir, Highly Honoured Sir, Councillor of War and Forests!

I have the honour of communicating to Your Right Honourable some further matters which came in with today's riding post from Mr. Glenck. I had already given the princely letter to the post when I received from His Serene Highness the Prince the command to add in a postscript what I here enclose in copy by way of extract. His Serene Highness believes that it may be of use to the same. His Most Serene Self finds himself better today than yesterday, inasmuch as the attack had withdrawn from the right hand into the left foot, and yesterday gave severe pain there; however this pain ceased during the night and was indeed, upon the stretching of the tendons,

no longer perceptible; we all hope for the best. Mr. Bernhardi, mining councillor, has arrived here, though as I myself saw yesterday — not altogether well — His Serene Highness sent me to set him at ease on that account, since He, on account of his continuing indisposition, had not yet been able to pay his respects. Your Right Honourable will permit me finally to append the most heartfelt wish for your recovery and for the most perfect and lasting health, and at the same time to be permitted to commend myself to your further and invaluable favour, ever in the most perfect veneration. Your Right Honourable's,

Breslau, the 8th of March

1805.

humble and obedient servant

A. Hahn

text_english:
Right Honourable Sir, Highly Honoured Sir, Councillor of War and Forests!

I have the honour of communicating to Your Right Honourable some further matters which came in with today's riding post from Mr. Glenck. I had already given the princely letter to the post when I received from His Serene Highness the Prince the command to add in a postscript what I here enclose in copy by way of extract. His Serene Highness believes that it may be of use to the same. His Most Serene Self finds himself better today than yesterday, inasmuch as the attack had withdrawn from the right hand into the left foot, and yesterday gave severe pain there; however this pain ceased during the night and was indeed, upon the stretching of the tendons,

no longer perceptible; we all hope for the best. Mr. Bernhardi, mining councillor, has arrived here, though as I myself saw yesterday — not altogether well — His Serene Highness sent me to set him at ease on that account, since He, on account of his continuing indisposition, had not yet been able to pay his respects. Your Right Honourable will permit me finally to append the most heartfelt wish for your recovery and for the most perfect and lasting health, and at the same time to be permitted to commend myself to your further and invaluable favour, ever in the most perfect veneration. Your Right Honourable's,

Breslau, the 8th of March

1805.

humble and obedient servant

A. Hahn
summary_en: Forwards further items arrived by that day's mounted post from Glenck, together with an extract in copy of a postscript ordered by His Serene Highness the Prince after the princely letter had already been posted, thought to be of use. Reports on the Prince's health: the attack has moved from the right hand to the left foot, painful the previous day but eased overnight. Notes Bergrath Bernhardi's arrival at Breslau in poor health, and wishes Triebenfeld recovery.
summary_de: Übersendet weitere mit der reitenden Post von Glenck eingegangene Nachrichten sowie einen vom Fürsten nachträglich befohlenen Auszug in Abschrift, den der fürstliche Brief nicht mehr aufnehmen konnte und der Triebenfeld nützlich sein dürfte. Berichtet über das Befinden Seiner Durchlaucht: der Anfall sei aus der rechten Hand in den linken Fuß gezogen, der Schmerz aber über Nacht gewichen. Bergrath Bernhardi sei in Breslau eingetroffen, jedoch unpäßlich und daher noch nicht zur Aufwartung fähig. Wünsche für Triebenfelds Genesung.
